info.timeAllocation:
Study hour (300h) = 105 contact hours (70 slots) + 2 hours final exam + 193 hours self-study

Interactive Classroom Teaching

1 slot =90'
info.description: This course is an advanced English course that refines learners’ ability to communicate with precision, fluency, and cultural sophistication in academic and professional settings. Students synthesize ideas from diverse authentic sources, analyze global and ethical issues, and evaluate meaning, bias, and rhetorical stance in complex spoken and written texts. Emphasis is placed on persuasive writing, academic discussion, and critical thinking. Learners apply technology and AI tools to enhance research and collaboration while demonstrating leadership, professionalism, and lifelong learning for global engagement.
info.studentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.

- Student is responsible for doing all exercises, assignments, and labs given by the instructor in class or at home and submitting them on time

- Use a laptop in class only for learning purposes

- Access the course website for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online support from teachers and other students, and for practicing and assessment.
info.note:
1) On-going assessment: 40%

2) Final Examination (FE): 60%

3) Final Result: 100%

4) Completion Criteria: On-going assessment >0, each part of final exam must be >0, Final Exam Score >=4/10 & Final Result >=5/10.

clos.loDetails: Identify and accurately use advanced English vocabulary, grammar, and pronunciation patterns in both academic and professional communication.
Synthesize and appraise cultural, social, and global perspectives from multiple authentic sources.
Interpret and critically evaluate nuanced meaning, bias, and rhetorical stance in lectures, debates, and multimedia; integrate key points from multiple spoken sources in summaries.
Express themselves fluently and spontaneously with precision and coherence, present complex ideas persuasively, and interact effectively in academic and professional discussions.
Analyze and interpret ideas, arguments, and rhetorical techniques from authentic texts demonstrating critical and inferential reading skills.
Compose clear, coherent, and well-structured essays, reports, and correspondence using advanced grammar, logical organization, and persuasive techniques.
Apply information technology and artificial intelligence (AI) tools to enhance research, collaboration, and language learning efficiently, ethically, and responsibly.
Work independently and collaboratively with accountability, demonstrating respect, leadership, professionalism, and ethical behavior in diverse academic and professional contexts.
Design and implement a personal learning plan using self-assessment, feedback, and technology to monitor progress and foster lifelong English learning and global engagement.

assessments.knowledgeSkill: Knowledge and skills in studied unit(s)
assessments.note:
In classroom
Combination of unit tests or progress tests and/or other activities

assessments.questionType: MC, multi response, matching, gap filling, completion; essay writing; open questions
assessments.noQuestion: 1. Listening: 25%Includes 2 parts, 20 questions.2. Reading: 25%Includes 2 articles; 20 questions.3. Writing: 25%Includes 250 words; 4-paragraph essay; type: opinion essay and advantage-disadvantage essay.4. Speaking: 25%Includes topics of units in the textbook.
assessments.note:
1. Listening:

20 questions; 2 audios; MCQ 4 options, gap filling, matching; level: B2+-C1; around 3-5 mins/audio; 2 times listening; ~25 minutes

2. Reading:

20 questions; 2 texts - 600-700 words/text; MCQ 4 options, gap filling, matching; level: B2+-C1; topic: 10 units in the textbook; 40 minutes

3. Writing:

at least 250 words, 4-5-paragraph essays - one topic; type: opinion essay and cause-solution essay; level: B2+-C1; 40 minutes

4. Speaking:

individually; 7 mins per student

Part 1. Long Run (1 min prep, 2-3 mins to speak)

1 minute to prepare

2–3 minutes to speak

Part 2. Discussion Questions (3 mins)

5 discussion questions provided

Teacher selects 1-2 questions to ask

Questions may be shuffled
